articles.title: Russell Wilson's horse, Club Reign, wins racing debut at Saratoga Race Track
articles.summary: Wilson and his wife Ciara are regulars at the Kentucky Derby.
articles.body:
Club Reign, a horse co-owned by former NFL quarterback Russell Wilson, won its debut race oSaturday at Saratoga Race Track. The 2-year-old colt won by 6 lengths during the opening race and paid $18.72 after going off as an 8-1 favorite.

"What a blessing, what a huge win," Wilson said afterward . "[Jockey] Edgard [Zayas] rocked it, [trainer] Whit Beckman, our team, Three Brand Racing racing. We're so excited. What a blessing, for sure, to do it here in Saratoga.

"We like winning big moments in New York. We won the Super Bowl here, we win this, it feels like the same feeling. … Club Reign was special."

After 14 years in the NFL with four teams, Wilson recently retired and is joining CBS Sports as a studio analyst this season .

Horse racing has long been an interest for the Super XLVIII winning quarterback. Wilson and his wife, singer Ciara, have been spotted at the Kentucky Derby the past several years.

According to Bloodhorse , Beckman lists Legion Bloodstock as one of his clients and when the group was introduced to Wilson's brother, Harry, who lives in Louisville, Kentucky, at last year's Run for the Roses, that's when the wheels were in motion for the longtime signal-caller to get into thoroughbred ownership.

Wilson and his team purchased a stake in Club Reign for $475,000 in April.

"Obviously," Wilson said , "there's nothing like holding that Lombardi Trophy in front of hundreds and hundreds of millions of people. … To win on Travers Day, to win in Saratoga first race out, it feels like [winning] Rookie of the Year."

Former MLBer Jayson Werth, who co-owns 2024 Belmont Stakes winner Doroch , is another former athlete that has a relationship with Legion.

articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football 2-Round Mock Draft Picks and Strategy Breakdown
articles.summary: The NFL's annual cutdown day is almost here. Teams must trim their rosters from 90 players to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, and from there, the preparation for Week 1 will begin.
articles.body:
The NFL's annual cutdown day is almost here. Teams must trim their rosters from 90 players to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, and from there, the preparation for Week 1 will begin.

Cutdown day also marks the opening of the prime fantasy draft window. The risk of preseason injuries will be minimal with exhibition games in the rear view. Managers will have a far better idea of players' roster status and projected roles once cuts are complete, too.

Information is valuable and can help managers craft a better strategy on draft day. Here, we'll discuss some early draft strategies while running through a 12-team, point-per-reception (PPR) mock draft conducted with FantasyPros' Mock Draft Simulator .

Christian McCaffrey, RB, San Francisco 49ers

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks

This mock draft began with a pair of running backs, Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson. This shouldn't come as a surprise, even though high-volume receivers like Ja'Marr Chase and Jaxon Smith-Njigba are popular picks to lead off Round 1.

The reality is that, this season, there's going to be a wide gap between first- and second-tier RBs and those available in the middle rounds. There simply aren't enough every-down backs left in the NFL to go around.

If the opportunity to draft a back like Gibbs, Robinson, Christian McCaffrey, or Jonathan Taylor presents itself, especially in the back half of Round 1, managers should take it. Otherwise, high-volume No. 1 receivers should rule the round.

However, managers may want to be a bit cautious with Atlanta Falcons receiver Drake London, who landed in the first round of this mock. London has been a productive receiver, but the Falcons face some big potential problems at quarterback. Michael Penix Jr. hasn't established himself as a quality starter, and Tua Tagovailoa has largely disappointed, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport:

Omarion Hampton, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Kansas City Chiefs

We saw another six running backs come off the board in Round 2, which shouldn't come as a surprise. While a handful of solid No. 1 receivers were still available—along with top-tier TEs Brock Bowers and Trey McBride—managers should expect to see an early run on RBs in 2026.

Backs like James Cook and Derrick Henry might not be elite-tier options, but they're going to be solid RB1s on most fantasy rosters.

Unfortunately, the bottom of Round 2 is where managers may decide to reach for RBs with strong bust potential. Kenneth Walker III falls firmly into this category. The reigning Super Bowl MVP has a solid ceiling as the Kansas City Chiefs' new starter. However, he carries some legitimate risk.

Walker appeared in all 17 games for the Seattle Seahawks this past season but has struggled to stay healthy in the past. He's also averaged fewer than eight combined touchdowns per season.

While Walker's upside is intriguing, managers can find better value in a back like the Los Angeles Rams' Kyren Williams, who went two rounds later than Walker in this mock.

As previously noted, this mock draft saw Round 2 come and go without Bowers or McBride getting drafted. With running backs carrying such a premium in 2026, this should be how many real-world fantasy drafts unfold.

Reaching for a TE or a QB in Round 2 could leave managers stuck in the RB wasteland that is Rounds 4-8. In the mock we examined, Williams and rookie Jeremiyah Love were the only RBs drafted in Rounds 3 and 4. Backs taken in the next tier—like Bucky Irving, Breece Hall, and Cam Skattebo—are highly volatile boom-or-bust prospects this year.

Managers who grabbed at least one starting RB in the first two rounds should look to continue adding WR talent in the middle rounds, as true No. 1 targets like Terry McLaurin and rookie Carnell Tate . This is also the correct point in the draft to go after top-tier TEs and quarterbacks like Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, and Drake Maye—if you're inclined to reach for a QB early.

We recommend waiting until after Round 6 to target a quarterback, as QBs like Dak Prescott, Matthew Stafford, and Justin Herbert should still be available. Managers who are eager to build around an elite QB, though, shouldn't do so before Round 3.

articles.title: Zac Taylor faces make-or-break season as Bengals rebuild defense around Joe Burrow's Super Bowl window
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals completely revamped their defense with Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen and Boye Mafe, but can Joe Burrow stay healthy?
articles.body: Few teams in the NFL are operating under as much pressure heading into the upcoming season as the Cincinnati Bengals. With head coach Zac Taylor facing intense scrutiny in his eighth season at the helm and defensive coordinator Al Golden entering year two of his unit's retool, Cincinnati is aiming to prove that its recent stagnation is over and that franchise quarterback Joe Burrow can lead them back to deep January football. Last year The Bengals suffered through a deeply disappointing 2025 season, stumbling to a 6–11 record and finishing dead last in a hyper-competitive AFC North. Burrow, again, got injured, and the team called on veteran Joe Flacco. They were good at times, but it always felt like this team had no real chance to earn the postseason spot. This was especially true when Burrow was out. A leaky, depleted defense completely unraveled at times, allowing opposing offenses to dictate games and squandering late leads. Defensive lapses and an inability to generate consistent pass-rush pressure made stringing together victories almost impossible, costing Cincinnati any realistic chance at a wild-card spot well before late December. ZAC TAYLOR ADMITS BREAKING NFL CHALLENGE FLAG RULE FOR 8 YEARS AS LEAGUE MAKES CHANGE Offseason additions and subtractions Recognizing that an elite offense was being wasted by defensive liabilities, the front office spent the offseason completely reshaping the front seven and secondary. The biggest marquee splash came via trade when Cincinnati acquired star defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence from the Giants, immediately pairing him with veteran pass rusher Jonathan Allen and edge Boye Mafe to fortify the interior line. In the secondary, the Bengals added physical safety help by signing Bryan Cook and Kyle Dugger, while re-signing reliable backup quarterback Joe Flacco alongside offensive tackle Orlando Brown Jr. and guard Dalton Risner. The aggressive retooling came with significant departures. On defense, the Bengals parted ways with longtime pass rusher Trey Hendrickson, edge Joseph Ossai, and defensive backs Cam Taylor-Britt, Geno Stone, and Marco Wilson. Hendrickson felt like the hardest to swallow, considering he went to the rival Ravens. Roster There is a valid reason for high-ceiling optimism when evaluating Cincinnati’s overall roster makeup. Offensively, as long as Joe Burrow stays healthy behind a re-signed offensive line, the Bengals boast one of the premier perimeter trios in the NFL with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins leading an explosive receiving group. Chase did hurt his knee in a non-contact play, but it appears he is okay. Still something worth being very concerned about if you're a fan or bettor. The primary difference-maker this season will be the defense. Under Al Golden's direction, the front seven transforms from a structural weakness into a potential strength. The combination of Lawrence and Allen stopping the run and pushing the pocket should create far easier third-down scenarios for a retooled secondary to capitalize on turnover opportunities. 4 NFL TEAMS TO INVEST IN AND SHORT AT THE SPORTSBOOKS AFTER THE 2026 REGULAR-SEASON SCHEDULE RELEASE SHOW Betting Outlook We’ve already seen what Burrow can do when healthy and equipped with even a decent defense. This is one of the few teams that stopped the Chiefs and made it to the Super Bowl. They fell short, but it gives an indication of just how good the team can be. There really shouldn’t be questions about the offense, but PFF has their offensive line ranked 20th in the league. If they can’t keep Burrow upright, how do they expect to win games? The good news for them is that they are ranked eighth in defensive line. Perhaps those changes in the offseason will give the Bengals a chance to win without Burrow being excellent, or even available for every game. Give me the Bengals to win the division at +184. articles.title: Colts QB Anthony Richardson Sr. hits Keenan Allen on first pass, has good day in QB2 battle
articles.summary: Anthony Richardson played a little less than a half in the preseason finale.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. doesn't know what the future holds for him. All he can do is take advantage of the opportunities he is given.

Richardson played well in the Colts' preseason finale on Saturday against the Detroit Lions. He got the start and went 7 of 10 for 80 yards before he was pulled for Riley Leonard midway through the second quarter. Richardson and Leonard are battling for the backup quarterback job behind Daniel Jones.

Richardson's day started very well. He found Keenan Allen, who recently signed with the Colts to bolster their receiver depth, for a nice 24-yard pass downfield. The play showed the best of Richardson, and also why the Colts signed the veteran Allen. It was a strong throw with plenty of velocity downfield and got the Colts immediately into Lions territory. Playing with a lineup of mostly backups, it was beneficial to Richardson to have at least one proven veteran to throw to on Saturday.

Richardson is still battling Leonard for the Colts' QB2 job, though Leonard hasn't played well in the preseason. Leonard did start over Richardson in the second preseason game. Richardson started the first and third games.

Richardson had a steady performance after that Allen pass. After the first drive ended with a field goal, the defense got a highlight from its star. Cornerback Sauce Gardner had a nice interception on a short pass, giving Richardson and the offense the ball back.

On the ensuing drive, Richardson missed badly on a throw to the end zone to set up a third-and-8, but then seemed to get a first down on an 11-yard pass. It was called back due to offensive pass interference. A short completion was short of the first down and set up another field goal.

Richardson was solid the rest of the day. It wasn't perfect but he didn't do anything to lose ground on the depth chart. Leonard didn't do much to move up; against the Lions he was 3 of 7 for 48 yards and an interception.

Richardson was the fourth pick of the 2023 NFL Draft and struggled, especially with his accuracy, and Jones replaced him as the team's starter. Richardson made a trade request in the offseason, but the Colts didn't move him. It's hard to know where Richardson's career goes from here, but at least he finished the preseason on a high note.

articles.title: Bills Re-Sod New Highmark Stadium Grass After NFL Player Calls Field 'Ass'
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are re-sodding the grass field at the new Highmark Stadium before Week 1 of the 2026 season, according to Lance Lysowski of the Buffalo News.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are re-sodding the grass field at the new Highmark Stadium before Week 1 of the 2026 season, according to Lance Lysowski of the Buffalo News .

The update comes after the original field conditions drew criticism, with one anonymous Bills player previously telling Tim Graham of The Athletic that "the field is ass right now."

Buffalo is using the new $2.2 billion stadium for the first time during its 2026 campaign after three years of construction.

The field contains Kentucky bluegrass grown at Tuckahoe Turf Farms in New Jersey (h/t Graham). Tuckahoe Turf Farms has also handled other NFL stadiums, including the Pittsburgh Steelers' Acrisure Stadium and the Philadelphia Eagles' Lincoln Financial Field.

While an official needed to stop the play clock to replace a divot on the field during the Bills' preseason opener, team president Pete Guelli didn't seem to have long-term concerns regarding the grass after the game.

"From a playability and safety perspective, everybody's very happy," Guelli said, per the Associated Press' John Wawrow . "It's Year 1. So it's a brand new field and it's going to take time for the foundation to build up. So some of the things people saw in the game, those will dissipate over time."

The Bills used artificial turf at their old Highmark Stadium, but switched to natural grass for their new home. It's worth noting that the NFL Players Association revealed on June 10 that 92 percent of NFL players prefer playing on natural grass over turf.

While the Bills will be on the road for a Week 1 matchup with the Houston Texans, their next three games of the 2026 season are set to take place at home.

articles.summary: Free-agent cornerback Terrion Arnold officially signed a deal with the Seattle Seahawks on Saturday.
articles.body:
Free-agent cornerback Terrion Arnold officially signed a deal with the Seattle Seahawks on Saturday.

Arnold will be placed on the commissioner's exempt list, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero:

Report: Seahawks All-Pro DT Gets $90M Deal

The new contract is expected to be a one-year deal, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Arnold visited the New York Giants, New Orleans Saints and Houston Texans before choosing to join the defending Super Bowl champions.

He became a free agent after he was released by the Detroit Lions in June.

Seattle's interest in Arnold was clear after his departure from Detroit, as the team hosted him for a visit on two separate occasions (via NFL insider Jordan Schultz ).

His workout for the Seahawks was also featured on Hard Knocks .

Devon Witherspoon and Josh Jobe are set to enter the 2026 season as Seattle's starting cornerbacks, but the team's No. 3 corner position is still up for grabs.

Noah Igbinoghene, Nehemiah Pritchett and third-round rookie Julian Neal are all potential candidates to earn the job. Now, Arnold could also challenge for the No. 3 spot.

He was initially selected by the Lions with the No. 24 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, appearing in 24 games across his first two seasons in Detroit. This included 22 starts.

Arnold racked up 91 tackles, 18 passes defended and one interception across both years. He allowed an 88.6 passer rating when targeted during his 2025 campaign, according to Pro Football Focus .

The Seahawks are looking to remain one of the NFL's top defensive squads this year after giving up a mere 17.2 points per game last season.

articles.title: NFL’s Decision on ‘End Racism’ Messages for 2026 Is Now Confirmed
articles.summary: The NFL will continue allowing teams to use “End Racism” messages during the 2026 season. The move follows last year’s Super Bowl, where “Choose Love” appear...
articles.body:
The NFL will continue allowing teams to use "End Racism" messages during the 2026 season. The move follows last year's Super Bowl, where "Choose Love" appeared instead, sparking questions about the future of the message.

The story goes back further. Colin Kaepernick 's 2016 protest pushed social justice into the center of the NFL debate. Ten years later, social justice issues remain part of the NFL conversation.

NFL Continues Commitment to Social Justice

The NFL will bring the "End Racism" message back to the field during the 2026 season. Teams can also use "Stop Hate," "Choose Love," and "Inspire Change" on the field, while players will have similar options for their helmet decals.

The message has been part of the NFL's social justice efforts since 2020. That year, the league began placing messages such as "End Racism" and "It Takes All of Us" in end zones. Players were also allowed to wear approved social justice messages on their helmets.

The NFL's Inspire Change initiative, launched in 2019, also became more visible during this period. The league continued working with players and teams on social justice programs and messages in the years that followed. "End Racism" was still available during the 2025 season, but it was not used at Super Bowl LIX on February 9, 2025, in New Orleans. Instead, "Choose Love" appeared in one end zone, while "It Takes All of Us" was used in the other.

That change drew attention because "End Racism" had been closely associated with the NFL's on-field messaging since 2020. Its absence from the Super Bowl, however, did not mean the league had dropped the phrase altogether.

NFL Senior Vice President of Social Responsibility Anna Isaacson explained the league's position, saying , "We're working hand-in-hand with players, and alongside our clubs, to amplify player voices and underscore what is most important to them. For decades, the NFL and its players have been a unifying force in American culture and society that brings people of all cultures and backgrounds together to enjoy America's most popular sport. This is an honor and responsibility that the league takes seriously, which is why we actively invest in off-field programs and on-field initiatives that promote unity."

"Choose Love" has also become a regular part of the NFL's messaging. The phrase gained wider attention after the Buffalo Bills began using it following the May 14, 2022, mass shooting at a supermarket in Buffalo. Isaacson also spoke about the continued use of "Choose Love," saying, "Choose Love continues to resonate across the league. It has become a unifying message of healing and hope, one that many players continue to wear voluntarily on helmet decals."

The decision keeps "End Racism" among the social messages available to NFL teams in 2026.

articles.title: “I’m Glad You Don’t Think So”: Titans QB Cam Ward Clashes With Reporter Over Preseason Performance Assessment
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward is struggling heavily as his second NFL season approaches. The mounting pressure seems to be getting to the sophomore Q...
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward is struggling heavily as his second NFL season approaches. The mounting pressure seems to be getting to the sophomore QB who did not have a great preseason. In two appearances, Ward has managed a disappointing 13 completions for 126 yards.

Even though the team won both games, Ward's inability to score has critics questioning whether he deserves the starting job. As the preseason comes to a close, Ward's poor play is the biggest talking point around the team.

When Nashville podcaster Jared Stillman asked Ward about his struggles on Thursday, the quarterback snapped back and asked the reporter how he thought it was going. The reporter flatly replied, "Not well."

Ward retorted: "I'm glad you don't think so. That's good."

But then, when the reporter asked again, Ward said:

"I assess it as, did we win the game, or did we lose a game? I assess it as what I can get better at. "I don't assess it as, someone who can get up there and operate when everything's on, it's a different process level," he added. "So, it's more of slowing down the game to everybody."

"I assess it as, did we win the game, or did we lose a game? I assess it as what I can get better at.

"I don't assess it as, someone who can get up there and operate when everything's on, it's a different process level," he added. "So, it's more of slowing down the game to everybody."

Ward also said that he is positive about the times ahead:

"And I believe we made a huge jump for week one and week two because we're getting more condensed in the playbook. We're not really opening everything up. And, when we come to week one, I think it will be a different story."

GM Mike Borgonzi brought in new head coach Robert Saleh, who has completely reconstructed both the player roster and the coaching staff. However, the starting offense is still out of sync, with Ward averaging a weak 6.9 yards per attempt and just 63 passing yards per game.

Specifically, Brian Daboll's offensive system should maximize Ward's running skills while teaching him how to read defenses. Meanwhile, Stillman warned that a fifth straight losing season could get Robert Saleh fired immediately

"And Robert Saleh in this situation could easily be one-and-done if this team doesn't show signs of improvement because the reason they hired him was his grand plan for Cam Ward…. I don't think he's popular enough to be able to survive it," Stillman said .

The Titans will kick off their 2026 regular season on September 13 against the New York Jets, Saleh's former team.

articles.title: Patriots make changes to running back room after Corey Kiner trade
articles.summary: The NFL’s 53-man roster deadline is set for Sunday at 6 p.m. ET.
articles.body:
After acquiring Corey Kiner from the Arizona Cardinals on the eve of the NFL's 53-man roster deadline, the New England Patriots thinned the backfield.

The organization announced the release of Hassan Haskins and have since cut JaMycal Hasty, per a Saturday report from Patriots on SI's Ethan Hurwitz .

Both running backs had signed ahead of the preseason opener after visiting Gillette Stadium for workouts.

Haskins, 26, entered the NFL with head coach Mike Vrabel's former Tennessee Titans in the fourth round of the 2022 draft at pick No. 131 overall. The past first-team All-Big Ten selection out of Michigan was claimed off waivers by the Los Angeles Chargers in 2024 and stands with 76 carries for 229 yards, 18 catches for 119 yards, three touchdowns and one start in his career. Through 371 snaps on offense and 683 snaps on special teams, the 6-foot-2, 228-pound back has handled 30 tackles and 28 kickoff returns.

Hasty, 29, broke into the league as an undrafted free agent in 2020. The 5-foot-8, 205-pound Baylor product was picked up by the San Francisco 49ers and rose from the practice squad to the active roster while in the NFC West. Stops with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Miami Dolphins have been accrued since then. As have stops in Foxborough through three coaching staffs, beginning as a waiver claim in 2023. Now 56 games in, Hasty's career includes 854 yards and six touchdowns across 181 touches from scrimmage. He has also returned 26 kickoffs.

As starters Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson looked on, the pair of vested veterans led the team rushing during the preseason finale against the Cleveland Browns. But the depth chart has added a No. 3 option in exchange for a 2028 seventh-round draft pick.

The reigning AFC champions made 15 reported cuts to begin the weekend. The NFL's cutdown deadline is set for Sunday at 6 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Dolphins HC Explains Why Success Won't Just Be 'Defined by Winning' Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins are rebuilding their roster and starting anew after bringing in new leadership in general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley. Miami has over $180 million in dead cap money for the 2026 season, per Over the Cap, making it exceedingly difficult to construct a competitive team.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins are rebuilding their roster and starting anew after bringing in new leadership in general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley. Miami has over $180 million in dead cap money for the 2026 season, per Over the Cap , making it exceedingly difficult to construct a competitive team.

Amid that backdrop, head coach Jeff Hafley said after the team's 17-12 preseason loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Friday that the team's success this year "is not just defined by winning" as the Dolphins look to create a foundation for the future.

"We, and I, want to win everything that we do. But success is not just defined by winning," Hafley said, per ESPN's Marcel-Louis Jacques . "We are going to compete. I want to win everything that we do. I've said that over and over. But at the same time, we need to make sure that this foundation and the process is built the right way. ... There's no shortcuts because it's bigger than that right now."

Hafley's comments were in response to a question from Louis-Jacques about his remarks on the Stephen A. Smith Show , in which the ESPN commentator asked the head coach how he would define success for the Dolphins this season. He provided this response (15:00 mark).

"Success...it's not going to be measured in wins and losses this year," Hafley started.

"And I know nobody wants to hear that. I want to see our team. I want to see where we end and how far we can take this thing and how much we develop these players and develop that image that I talked to you about. Success for me is gonna to be we go on that field, and we play so damn hard where even you turn it on and say, 'Man, those guys are flying around. They're playing together. They love each other. They're in this thing together,' and we're just growing and building and growing and building, and we'll see where this takes us.

"I just, going to stay away from the win-loss total. I just think this year is so much about developing who we are as a football team, finding the right guys, and then just by the end of the year, saying, 'You know what? We got something really powerful going forward.'"

The projections for the 2026 season are low. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , they have 500-1 odds to win the Super Bowl, longer than any other team aside from the Arizona Cardinals (1000-1). A bettor would get plus odds just to choose the Dolphins to win five or more games ( +145 ).

Of course, time will tell how Miami does. We'll see how the Dolphins' season goes soon enough beginning Sunday, Sept. 13, when Miami visits the Las Vegas Raiders.

articles.title: New Raiders Rumors Reveal Kirk Cousins, Fernando Mendoza QB1 Decision Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will start out his first NFL season backing up veteran signal caller Kirk Cousins.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will start out his first NFL season backing up veteran signal caller Kirk Cousins.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is expected to name Cousins the team's starter for Week 1 of the 2026 season, according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports.

Cousins joined the Raiders in early April on a de facto one-year, $20 million deal, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Later that month, the Raiders used the No. 1 pick of the 2026 NFL draft to select Mendoza out of Indiana.

Kubiak said in May whether Cousins, Mendoza or Aidan O'Connell would start the season as QB1 would "reveal itself" over OTAs and minicamp.

He named Cousins the starter ahead of training camp but said he wanted Mendoza and O'Connell "to push" Cousins for the job.

Mendoza got a chance to make that push during an Aug. 14 preseason matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, during which he became the first top pick since Baker Mayfield to throw a touchdown pass in his preseason debut.

Kubiak ultimately decided to go with the more experienced option by turning to Cousins ahead of Week 1.

Cousins played with a younger quarterback during his recent stint with the Atlanta Falcons, where he signed in 2024 shortly before the franchise used a first-round pick on Michael Penix Jr.

With the Falcons, Cousins struggled while playing through injury late in the 2024 season before losing his starting job to Penix.

He ultimately came back to start eight games for the Falcons in 2025, completing 61.7 percent of his passes for 1,721 passing yards with 10 touchdowns and five interceptions as Penix dealt with injuries and inconsistency.

Unlike in Atlanta , where his former team surprised him by using a first-round pick on Michael Penix Jr., Cousins signed in Las Vegas knowing he would be competing with a rookie for the job.

Kubiak will now hope starting Cousins can give Mendoza more time to learn behind a veteran quarterback before the former Indiana star sees his first NFL action.

articles.title: Lil Wayne Disses Ben Johnson Shirtless Video, Bears, Lions, Vikings in 'Special Ops' Packers Song
articles.summary: Lil Wayne mocked the viral video of Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson's shirtless postgame celebration in his new hype song for the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Lil Wayne mocked the viral video of Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson's shirtless postgame celebration in his new hype song for the Green Bay Packers.

The rapper called out Johnson alongside the rest of the NFC North in his new song "Special Ops."

Lil Wayne first referenced Johnson with the lyrics "We gon' ball till we fall and get back up / If the coach in Chicago want act up" (h/t AZ Lyrics ).

He later added: "Tell your coach put his shirt back on / I got bear fur on my floor at home / We gon' make you eat all them words / And may they taste like provolone."

Johnson ripped off his shirt following a postgame speech in the Bears' locker room following a Black Friday win over the Philadelphia Eagles. He later said he went shirtless because the hot dog stand The Wieners Circle had promised to give out free hot dogs if he did so.

The Bears weren't the only division rivals to take a hit in Lil Wayne's new song.

The rapper said the Packers had the "NFC division crown on" before adding "Don't you know this enemy turf you on? / We don't do Honolulu blue / And don't come in here with no purple on."

Lil Wayne concluded, "The Bears still suck / The Vikings still drunk / The Lions tails tucked."

The Bears beat the Packers in the regular season on their way to winning the NFC North title last season, then defeated the Packers in the Wild Card round to eliminate their rivals from the playoffs.

Lil Wayne will hope his new song gives the Packers a boost as the team looks to earn redemption over the Bears and reclaim its division title starting with a season-opening Sept. 13 road game against the Minnesota Vikings.

articles.title: Cowboys, Steelers Make Surprise Trade in New NFL Rumors Ahead of Roster Cutdown Deadline
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are reportedly moving on from offensive tackle Broderick Jones ahead of the final season of his expiring rookie contract.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are reportedly moving on from offensive tackle Broderick Jones ahead of the final season of his expiring rookie contract.

The Steelers are trading Jones to the Dallas Cowboys, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Saturday.

The Cowboys also acquired a fourth-rounder in the trade while sending third-round and sixth-round picks to the Steelers, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

The Cowboys also released wide receiver Denzel Mims Saturday, according to Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News.

The moves come after Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday outside linebacker Marist Liufau had suffered a fractured forearm necessitating surgery.

The Cowboys could use one of two IR spots for Liufau if he is expected to miss at least the first four games of the season.

Jones, the No. 14 pick of the 2023 draft, played the first three seasons of his NFL career for the Steelers.

He started 11 games in 2025 before he was shut down for the season with a neck injury.

Jones arrives in Dallas having played in 45 games with 38 career starts for the Steelers.

The Steelers declined the fifth-year option on Jones' rookie contract earlier this spring.

The decision took place after Schefter reported in April that Jones had suffered a "setback" in his recovery from his neck injury.

Jones was sidelined for most of the offseason. He was cleared in time for training camp but struggled at points in the preseason, including when he gave up two sacks in an Aug. 21 matchup against the New York Jets.

Jones started the 2025 campaign as the Steelers' starting left tackle, but that position was taken when the team moved Troy Fautanu to left tackle earlier this offseason.

The Steelers also drafted right tackle Max Iheanachor in the first round of the 2026 draft, further calling into question Jones' future with the team.

The Cowboys currently have Tyler Guyton seemingly as a lock at left tackle. Jones could potentially provide some competition for Terence Steele at right tackle once he arrives in Dallas.

The NFL roster cutdown deadline is Sunday at 6 p.m. ET. The Cowboys will need to decide where Jones fits in the team's tackle depth chart before opening the season Sept. 13 at the New York Giants.
